sentence_stem: If only I had left earlier,
correct_completion: I would not have missed the train.
full_sentence: If only I had left earlier, I would not have missed the train.
acceptable_variants: I would have arrived on time.
I would have caught the bus.

options.why_wrong: This describes the present, but the stem uses the past perfect 'had left', which needs a past result.
This describes the bus, not the result of leaving earlier, so it does not complete the unreal past wish.

options.text: I would not have missed the train.

options.why_wrong: This is a future plan, not an unreal past result, so it does not match the 'if only' structure.

explanation: 'If only' with the past perfect expresses regret about an unreal past situation. The main clause uses would have plus a past participle to show the imagined result. Polish speakers may use a simple conditional here because the past perfect is not used in the same way in their first language.
translation: Gdybym tylko wyszedł wcześniej, nie spóźniłbym się na pociąg.
